summary:
## The Core Concept: Swapping Claude's Engine

The main idea is to use the **Claude Code agentic framework** (the "F1 car") but replace the expensive default AI model with a free or cheaper alternative (the "engine") via **OpenRouter**. This gives you access to the powerful coding environment and skills of Claude Code without the high cost.

## Key Trade-Offs When Choosing a Model

When switching from the default Claude models, you must consider the balance between four key factors:

- **Cost**: Ranging from free to a fraction of Claude Opus's price.
- **Performance**: How capable and intelligent the model is.
- **Speed**: The response time of the model.
- **Security**: The data handling policies of the model provider.

## Recommended Model Alternatives

- **Claude Opus/Sonnet**: The benchmark for performance and quality. Best for professional or client work.
- **Gemini Flash**: A great value proposition, offering ~85% of Opus's performance for ~10% of the cost. Ideal for large projects where token costs are a concern.
- **Free Models (e.g., DeepSeek, Mistral)**: Excellent for experimenting or if you've hit credit limits, but be prepared for lower performance and potential rate-limiting.

> [!TIP]
> When using the free tier, select the `open-router/auto` model. This will automatically cycle through available free models, helping you avoid getting stuck on a single one that is being rate-limited.

## Step-by-Step Setup Guide

1.  **Select Your Model**: Choose a model based on the cost/performance trade-off that suits your needs.
2.  **Create an OpenRouter API Key**: Go to `OpenRouter.ai`, create a new API key, and name it.
    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > It's highly recommended to deposit a small amount (e.g., $10) into your OpenRouter account. This helps avoid rate-limiting issues, even when using free models, ensuring a much smoother experience.
3.  **Configure in Antigravity**: Open the **Antigravity** IDE, create a new project folder, and paste the provided prompt (from the video's companion site) into the agent window. The agent will ask for your OpenRouter API key and automatically update your `settings.json` file.
4.  **Test and Verify**: Restart the terminal in Antigravity (`File > New Terminal`). Run the `claude` command and ask "What model is this?" to confirm that you are now using your selected model (e.g., Gemini).
5.  **Revert to Default**: To switch back to Claude Opus, use the specific "reset" prompt provided. This will restore the original configuration.

## Key Takeaways & Best Practices

- **Skill Portability**: All your existing **Claude Skills** are portable and will work with the new models. This is a huge advantage if you run out of credits but still need to use your custom tools.
- **Session Management**: In Antigravity, you can open multiple terminals or agent windows. It's good practice to have one window for controlling/switching models and other windows for your actual coding work.
- **False Economies**: Remember that **free doesn't always mean cheaper**. The time you spend correcting mistakes or waiting for a slower free model can be more costly than paying for a premium one. Use the free/cheap options strategically.
- **Personal Recommendation**: If affordable, the **Claude Max plan** is seen as a powerful investment—hiring a "mini digital employee" that can dramatically accelerate development and automation.
